advances: Supplies a dimension-independent lower bound on maximal halfspace depth from relative entropy to a log-concave reference measure. This is a probability input for the reflected midpoint route, not a proof of the locked mixed-integer conjecture.
author: research-agent
external_sources: László Lovász and Santosh Vempala, [The Geometry of Logconcave Functions and Sampling Algorithms](https://faculty.cc.gatech.edu/~vempala/papers/logcon.pdf), Lemma 5.12, printed page 24 of the author manuscript; [journal DOI: 10.1002/rsa.20135](https://doi.org/10.1002/rsa.20135). The lemma states: for a log-concave probability density \(h\) on \(\mathbb R^d\) with centroid \(\mathbf c\), every halfspace \(H\) containing \(\mathbf c\) satisfies \(\int_Hh(\mathbf y)\,d\mathbf y\ge1/e\). We apply it to \(h=g_s\) and \(H=H_s\). Normalization, log-concavity, finite first moment, and containment of the centroid were checked above. No continuity, compact support, or isotropic normalization of the conditional reference density is needed. The entropy estimate is proved directly above and uses no external information-theoretic theorem.
proof:
For \(\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(\mathbf u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\), put \(H(\mathbf x,\mathbf u):=\{\mathbf y:\langle\mathbf u,\mathbf y-\mathbf x\rangle\ge0\}\). Every closed halfspace containing \(\mathbf x\) contains one of these through-\(\mathbf x\) halfspaces. The map \((\mathbf x,\mathbf u)\mapsto P(H(\mathbf x,\mathbf u))\) is continuous: along any convergent sequence of its arguments, the halfspace indicators converge except on the limiting boundary hyperplane, which has \(P\)-measure zero, and dominated convergence applies. Compactness of \(\mathbb S^{d-1}\) therefore gives \(\operatorname{TD}_P(\mathbf x)=\min_{\mathbf u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}P(H(\mathbf x,\mathbf u))\). This minimum is continuous in \(\mathbf x\): locally the preceding continuous map is uniformly continuous on the product of a compact neighborhood and the sphere, so taking its minimum preserves continuity.

The set \(K:=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{supp}P)\) is compact. Strict separation shows that every \(\mathbf x\notin K\) has a through-\(\mathbf x\) halfspace disjoint from \(K\), hence has depth zero. Since \(f\) integrates to one, it is positive somewhere. Continuity bounds \(f\) below by a positive constant on a ball about such a point, and every halfspace through the center contains half that ball. The center thus has positive depth. Consequently the global maximum is positive and is attained on \(K\). Opposite halfspaces through any point have masses summing to one, because their common hyperplane is null. Thus \(0<\Delta\le1/2\).

Set \(r:=\lfloor1/(2\Delta)\rfloor\). Since \(1/(2\Delta)\ge1\) and \(\lfloor t\rfloor\ge t/2\) for \(t\ge1\), we have \(1/(4\Delta)\le r\le1/(2\Delta)\), in particular \(r\ge1\).

We construct convex Borel sets \(A_0,\ldots,A_r\), starting from \(A_0=\mathbb R^d\). Suppose \(0\le s<r\) and \(P(A_s)\ge1-s\Delta\ge1/2\). Absolute continuity \(P\ll Q\) implies \(Q(A_s)>0\). The conditional measure \(Q_s:=Q(\,\cdot\mid A_s)\) has density \(g_s:=g\mathbf1_{A_s}/Q(A_s)\). This density is log-concave because \(A_s\) is convex, and its first absolute moment is at most \(Q(A_s)^{-1}\int\|\mathbf y\|g(\mathbf y)\,d\mathbf y<\infty\). Its centroid \(\mathbf c_s:=\int\mathbf y\,g_s(\mathbf y)\,d\mathbf y\) is therefore well-defined.

Choose a minimizing direction at \(\mathbf c_s\), and let \(H_s\) be the resulting closed halfspace through \(\mathbf c_s\). Then \(P(H_s)=\operatorname{TD}_P(\mathbf c_s)\le\Delta\). This uses only the global definition of \(\Delta\); the centroid need not lie in the support of \(P\). The log-concave centroid halfspace inequality, stated in EXTERNAL SOURCES, gives \(Q_s(H_s)\ge e^{-1}\). Define \(A_{s+1}:=A_s\setminus H_s\), a convex Borel set since it is the intersection of \(A_s\) with an open halfspace. We obtain

\[
\begin{aligned}
P(A_{s+1})
&\ge P(A_s)-P(H_s)\ge1-(s+1)\Delta,\\
Q(A_{s+1})
&=Q(A_s)(1-Q_s(H_s))\le(1-e^{-1})Q(A_s).
\end{aligned}
\]

These estimates justify every step of the induction, including positivity of the next conditioning mass by \(P\ll Q\). At its end, \(p:=P(A_r)\ge1/2\) and \(0<q:=Q(A_r)\le(1-e^{-1})^r=e^{-\ell r}<1\).

For completeness, write \(w=dP/dQ\). Jensen's inequality for \(t\log t\), first under \(Q\) conditioned on \(A_r\) and then under \(Q\) conditioned on its complement, yields \(D\ge p\log(p/q)+(1-p)\log((1-p)/(1-q))\). We use \(0\log0=0\), so this also holds when \(p=1\). Since \(p\log p+(1-p)\log(1-p)\ge-\log2\) and \((1-p)\log(1/(1-q))\ge0\), it follows that

\[
\begin{aligned}
D+\log2
&\ge p\log(1/q)\\
&\ge \frac{\ell r}{2}\\
&\ge \frac{\ell}{8\Delta}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Also \(D\ge0\) by Jensen under \(Q\), using \(\int w\,dQ=1\). Rearrangement gives the asserted bound at the attained maximizer. All hyperplanes are null for both original measures and their conditional densities, so the use of closed cutting halfspaces and open remainders introduces no boundary mass.
statement:
Let \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), and let \(P,Q\) be probability measures on \(\mathbb R^d\) with Lebesgue densities \(f,g\), respectively. Assume that \(f\) is continuous and compactly supported, that \(g\) is log-concave with \(\int\|\mathbf y\|g(\mathbf y)\,d\mathbf y<\infty\), and that \(P\ll Q\) with finite relative entropy \(D:=D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|Q)=\int\log(dP/dQ)\,dP\). All logarithms are natural. Define \(\operatorname{TD}_P(\mathbf x):=\inf\{P(H):H\text{ is a closed halfspace containing }\mathbf x\}\), \(\Delta:=\sup_{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^d}\operatorname{TD}_P(\mathbf x)\), and \(\ell:=-\log(1-e^{-1})\).

There exists \(\mathbf x^\star\in\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{supp}P)\) attaining \(\Delta\), and \(\operatorname{TD}_P(\mathbf x^\star)=\Delta\ge\ell/[8(D+\log2)]\). In particular, the maximizer lies in any compact convex set supporting \(P\).
